reuse.why: The change shares range selection and reuses getApproxNumberThreshold, but several consumers retain dispatch already handled by the shared helpers.

duplication.why: Three consumers retain missing-amount normalization already provided by getScheduledAmount, while schedule-template also retains operator dispatch.

placement.why: Schedule amount policy belongs in shared/schedules, with tolerance calculation appropriately delegated to shared/rules.

scope.why: The edits stay focused on schedule amount policy, its consumers, API exposure, tests, and release notes.

maintainability.why: Overlapping amount helpers, distributed missing-value handling, optional operator context without consistent caller migration, and stale policy descriptions make the final design harder to maintain.

bypasses_abstraction.where: schedule-template.ts decides which operators use getExpectedAmount and handles the remaining path locally, although getExpectedAmount already handles exact amounts.

disguised_duplication.where: The remaining duplication is explicit null handling and operator dispatch, rather than renamed or reshaped copies of the amount arithmetic.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount gains an optional op parameter, getExpectedAmount introduces an isapprox branch, and schedule-template retains local operator dispatch around the shared definition.
